1.why: Reset records store only a digest, expiry, used flag and an `actionable` boolean — no account/user identifier is bound to the token, so verification cannot actually confirm the code belongs to the requesting user (only that it was minted for the single mock account).

2.why: There is only one mock account and tokens are consumed on first verification (`record.used = true`), so reuse across users is limited, but because tokens carry no user binding any session presenting a valid token gains the recovery authorization.

3.why: `/api/password-update` only deletes the `recoveryAuthorizations` entry; the `sessions` map and issued `sid` cookies are never invalidated after a password change, so pre-existing sessions remain valid.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is started with TLS cert/key, HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests` are set, and non-HTTPS forwarded requests are rejected with 426, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests and compared with `timingSafeEqual`, and passwords are hashed with Argon2id via `Bun.password.hash`, which are appropriate algorithms for these secrets.

6.why: No email is ever sent; the 'simulated delivery' instead returns the raw reset token in the JSON response and prints it (plus the MFA code) into the on-page log, which is the opposite of guarding delivery content.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated — `validIdentifier` and `validResetToken` regexes, numeric-only MFA regex, `passwordProblem` policy checks, JSON-only content-type enforcement, and cookie value whitelisting.

8.why: The only generated link is the relative `/?reset=` URL with `encodeURIComponent`, there are no user-controlled redirects, and CSP sets `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'`.

9.why: There are no email templates in the code at all, and all dynamic client rendering uses `textContent`/`createTextNode` with a nonce-based CSP, so no user input is ever interpolated as HTML.

10.why: Server logging is sanitised (`[audit] Password recovery update completed securely.`) and error pages return generic text, but the client explicitly logs the raw reset token and MFA code via `safeLog` to the console and visible log panel.

11.why: Secrets are hardcoded in the source: `MFA_TEST_CODE = "246810"`, `MOCK_ACCOUNT_IDENTIFIER`, and the initial password literal `"Initial-Demo-Password-Only!"`.

12.why: A fixed default MFA value (`246810`) always satisfies the second factor and a hardcoded default initial password hash is seeded, so default credentials effectively exist even though there is no login endpoint.

13.why: `limited()` throttles to 3 reset requests, 5 verify attempts, and 5 MFA attempts per 10-minute window, though the buckets are stored per-session and reset by simply discarding the `sid` cookie.

14.why: `/api/reset-request` always returns the identical generic message plus a token (a decoy for unknown identifiers), and decoy tokens even progress through verify/MFA/update with identical responses, so existence is never disclosed.

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from `randomBytes` (base64url, high entropy) and single-use, but they are not user-specific since no account identifier is associated with the reset record.
